question: What are the three main parts of the epidemiological triangle used to study diseases?
explanation: Think of disease as a puzzle with three pieces: the agent (the germ), the host (the person), and the environment (where they meet). They all work together! [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h1)

question: A patient's body is weak and poorly nourished, making it easy for infections to take hold. In the epidemiological triangle, what is this person considered?
explanation: You've got this! The host is simply the living organism (like a human patient) that the germ settles inside. Things like nutrition and immunity determine how easily the host gets sick. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h1)

question: When a nurse puts on gloves before touching blood, which part of the chain of infection is being blocked?
explanation: Great job thinking about safety! Gloves act as a physical wall, stopping germs from jumping out of a patient or getting onto your skin. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h2)

question: A patient with active tuberculosis coughs openly in a packed hospital ward. How is this infection mainly traveling to other people?
explanation: Those tiny droplets flying through the air act as the vehicle—or mode of transmission—carrying the germ straight to someone else. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h2)

question: In the clinic, which patients should you use standard precautions for?

options.A: Surgical patients in the theatre only

explanation: Always treat every patient's blood and body fluids as if they could be infectious. Safety first for everyone, every time! [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h3)

question: What special kind of room ventilation do you need for a patient placed on airborne precautions?
explanation: A negative pressure room acts like a trap—it keeps the bad air inside and stops germs from floating out into the hallway when the door opens. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the main difference between disinfection and sterilization?

options.A: Disinfection takes longer to complete than sterilization
options.B: Sterilization uses chemical liquids, while disinfection uses heat
options.C: Disinfection is used on skin, while sterilization is for floors
options.D: Sterilization destroys bacterial spores, while disinfection does not

explanation: Sterilization is the ultimate clean—it kills everything, even tough little spores. Disinfection cleans most things, but some hardy spores might survive. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h4)

question: You clean a patient's skin with povidone-iodine right before putting in an IV line. What is this process called?
explanation: When you use a chemical to clean living skin and stop germs from growing, you are doing antisepsis! (Disinfectants are for tables, antiseptics are for skin). [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h4)

question: An infant gets ready-made antibodies through breast milk. What type of immunity is this?
explanation: Because the baby didn't have to fight the germs themselves to make the antibodies (they got them naturally from mum), it's natural passive immunity! [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is getting a large percentage of the community vaccinated so important for vulnerable people?

options.A: It guarantees lifelong active immunity for infants
options.C: It prevents the mutation of bacterial cell walls

explanation: When almost everyone is vaccinated, the disease has nowhere to hide or travel. This 'herd immunity' protects the few babies or sick folks who can't get vaccinated. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the main goal of antimicrobial stewardship programs in the hospital?

options.A: To optimize the use of antimicrobial drugs
options.B: To completely eliminate the need for antibiotics
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital pharmacy stock
options.D: To speed up the manufacturing of new vaccines

explanation: Stewardship is all about using the right drug, at the right dose, for the right time—so we beat the infection without creating superbug resistance. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h6)

question: A patient stops taking their antibiotics after three days because their fever is gone. As a nurse, what should you do?

options.A: Discard the remaining tablets in the clinical waste bin
options.B: Explain the importance of completing the full prescription course
options.C: Document that the patient is fully cured of the infection
options.D: Prescribe a secondary broad-spectrum drug to prevent relapse

explanation: Always gently remind patients to finish their drugs! Stopping early lets the strongest germs survive and bounce back even stronger. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the simple difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine separates exposed people
options.B: Isolation is used for bacteria, while quarantine is for viral infections
options.C: Isolation is voluntary, whereas quarantine is legally enforced
options.D: Quarantine requires negative pressure, while isolation uses standard rooms

explanation: Easy to remember: Isolation is for those who are already sick, while quarantine is for healthy people who were exposed and need to wait out the incubation period. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h7)

question: A healthy traveler arrives from a country with an active disease outbreak and is asked to stay at home for 14 days. What is this called?
explanation: Spot on! Since they feel fine right now but were exposed, keeping them at home for 14 days to watch for symptoms is quarantine. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of public health disease surveillance?

options.A: To calculate monthly hospital revenue and bed turnover
options.B: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on healthy populations
options.C: To evaluate individual nursing staff clinical performance
options.D: To monitor disease trends and guide timely control measures

explanation: Surveillance is like keeping watch over the horizon. Tracking disease patterns helps health teams spot outbreaks early and stop them fast. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h8)

question: A case of cholera is confirmed in a community. Which nursing action helps manage and stop the outbreak?

options.A: Administering surgical operations for chronic abdominal pain
options.B: Discharging all stable patients to reduce ward congestion
options.C: Tracing contacts and educating the community on safe water use
options.D: Ordering immediate laboratory upgrades for the regional hospital

explanation: To stop cholera, you have to track down who else might be infected and teach people how to keep their water and surroundings safe! [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h8)
